extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: A vision-dependent multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 human-selected samples for evaluating large vision-language models. It covers six core capabilities and eighteen detailed axes, with 250 samples per core capability and a relatively even distribution across the detailed axes. Samples are curated for visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and advanced multi-modal reasoning requirements.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.citeAs: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, and Feng Zhao. Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? Preprint, arXiv:2403.20330v2 [cs.CV], 9 April 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples were collected from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: SEED, MMBench, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista. An automated pipeline used eight LLM inspectors to filter an initial pool of 22,401 samples, retaining 11,607 candidates answered correctly by no more than two inspectors without visual input. Sixteen LVLMs were then used to estimate sample difficulty. Three experts conducted manual review and selected 1,500 samples, considering visual dependency, capability coverage, and difficulty diversity.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: An initial pool of 22,401 evaluation samples from SEED and MMBench, which focus on natural images, and MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista, which focus on scientific and technical knowledge. The evaluated source subsets are SEED-Image, MMBench-EN-Dev, MMMU-Val, ScienceQA-Test, AI2D-Test, and MathVista-Mini.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All questions were converted into a multiple-choice format. The final sample selection balances the six core capability dimensions at 250 samples each and maintains a relatively even distribution across eighteen detailed axes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two closed-source LLMs and six open-source LLMs of at least 20B parameters inspected samples using text-only inputs. The open-source inspectors used a 2-shot in-context inference strategy to reduce response refusals and ensure consistent answer formatting. Samples answered correctly by more than two of the eight inspectors were excluded. The retained samples were evaluated by sixteen LVLMs and assigned difficulty categories by correct-answer counts: easy (12–16), moderate (8–11), hard (4–7), and tough (0–3). Manual review reduced the retained pool to 1,500 samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts manually reviewed the coarsely filtered samples to ensure that answers depended on understanding visual content, that the selection covered a comprehensive range of capability dimensions, and that most samples required advanced multi-modal abilities. The benchmark organizes samples into six core capability dimensions and eighteen detailed axes consolidated from existing benchmarks. The paper does not specify how answer labels were originally authored or whether they were revised.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The manual reviewers are described as three experts; no further demographic specifications are provided.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automated text-only inspection used GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Mixtral-8x7B, Deepseek-67B, LLaMA2-70B, and Qwen1.5-72B. Sixteen LVLMs supplied correct-answer counts used to assign sample difficulty categories.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain visual dependency and reduce accidental leakage into LLM and LVLM training corpora. No update schedule, versioning policy, named maintainers, or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper argues that visually unnecessary evaluation samples and unintentional training-data leakage can cause unfair model comparisons, misrepresent actual multi-modal performance gains, and misguide LVLM research. MMStar and the proposed metrics aim to support more transparent, equitable, and reliable evaluation based on models' ability to integrate and interpret multi-modal data rather than memorize specific samples.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark targets minimal rather than zero data leakage. Across the evaluated LVLMs, MMStar's average multi-modal leakage metric was 1.9, with some models exhibiting higher leakage.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking LVLM multi-modal capabilities across coarse perception, fine-grained perception, instance reasoning, logical reasoning, science and technology, and mathematics. Evaluation uses accuracy, multi-modal gain (MG), and multi-modal leakage (ML). MG is the score with visual inputs minus the score without visual inputs; ML is the maximum of zero and the difference between the LVLM's text-only score and its LLM backbone's score. The paper evaluates LLMs on MMStar with a 2-shot strategy and LVLMs with a 0-shot strategy. Heuristic matching rules are used to score multiple-choice answers.
